pathway.title: ENCORE CAPITAL GROUP INC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. Leverage fell on the company's own measure while debt rose. Evidence: total debt to Adjusted EBITDA moved from 5.96x at FY2025 to 5.13x at Q3 2026 on a last twelve months basis, with principal debt rising from USD 4,033,394 thousand to USD 4,267,981 thousand and last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA rising from USD 676,958 thousand to USD 831,829 thousand [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: the gain comes from earnings growth, not from debt reduction. Credit implication: leverage is falling because collections are strong; it would rise again if earnings fell, since debt is not being repaid. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading.

2. Cash interest cover improved and is adequate on a last twelve months basis. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA over cash paid for interest was 3.07x at Q3 2026 against 2.61x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: cash interest is paid on semi-annual coupon dates, so single quarters mislead and the last twelve months basis is the right one. Credit implication: debt service is covered more than three times on the company measure, but the measure is before the portfolio purchases that sustain collections. Category: Documentary Fact.

3. Revolver headroom narrowed after the convertible settlement. Evidence: issuer-stated availability under the Global Senior Facility moved from USD 814.3 million at FY2025 to USD 510.2 million at Q3 2026, the revolver draw rose from USD 691,648 thousand at Q2 2026 to USD 974,763 thousand at Q3 2026, and utilisation was 65.6% against 42.6% at FY2025; the other facilities are drawn to their commitments [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: purchases, refinancing and share repurchases are all funded from the revolver, and the loan to value covenant applies once utilisation exceeds 20%, so it is live. Credit implication: liquidity is thinner than a year ago and covenant headroom cannot be measured. Category: Documentary Fact; the covenant gap is Insufficient Information.

4. Adjusted EBITDA quality is the central definition risk. Evidence: nine month 2026 changes in recoveries of USD 244,898 thousand are 38.0% of nine month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 644,320 thousand, and are deducted as non-cash in operating cash flow of USD 159,630 thousand, while purchases of USD 1,187,072 thousand sit in investing cash flow [CP-1]; management concluded over-performance did not represent a material shift in timing, which is Management Language [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk]. Risk mechanic: revenue depends on forecast revisions that can reverse. Credit implication: headline leverage and cover overstate the cash left for debt service after reinvestment. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

5. The maturity profile is long but concentrated in 2029. Evidence: no instrument in the notes tables matures before 2028, USD 331.6 million of sterling notes matures in 2028, and USD 1424.8 million (the revolver and the U.S. facility) matures in 2029 [CP-1]; the 2026 refinancings replaced the 9.250% 2029 notes with 6.625% 2032 notes and extended the U.S. facility to October 2029 [CP-1A: Transaction summary]. Risk mechanic: the largest refinancing step is the secured bank-style funding that also supports daily purchasing. Credit implication: refinancing risk is back-ended but a single event, the 2029 renewal of both the revolver and the U.S. facility, matters. Category: Documentary Fact.

6. Business risk centres on pricing, forecasts and the legal channel. Evidence: the business is dominated by debt purchasing revenue, United States purchasing is funded largely by forward flow agreements with a minimum commitment of USD 684.5 million, cost of legal collections rose 25.7% for nine months 2026 on higher US legal placements, and no material legal reserves are recorded [CP-1A: Revenue streams, Q3 2026], [CP-1A: Forward flow commitments], [CP-1A: Cost structure]. Risk mechanic: pricing and forecast errors flow into revenue; legal collections carry court cost and conduct risk. Credit implication: earnings are sensitive to collection performance and regulation, and seller concentration is Insufficient Information. Category: Documentary Fact; seller concentration is Insufficient Information.

7. Governance gives creditors no sponsor support and no sponsor extraction. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder is named, there is no dividend history, share repurchases of USD 89.5 million in 2025 and USD 73.4 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 are expected to be funded partly from the revolver, and the refinancing record is repeated [CP-1A: Ownership and control], [CP-1A: Distributions]. Risk mechanic: shareholder returns compete with deleveraging for revolver capacity. Credit implication: capital allocation is a monitoring point; behaviour is Neutral or Mixed on documented actions only. Category: Documentary Fact for the actions, Analyst Interpretation for the behaviour label.

cells.text: Buys portfolios of defaulted consumer receivables at deep discounts and works with consumers to repay; also provides debt servicing in Europe.
10-K page:4 "We primarily purchase portfolios of defaulted consumer receivables at deep discounts to face value"
Earnings come from collecting more than the price paid; purchase pricing is the main value driver, so a pricing error shows up in later forecast cuts and revenue.
MCM (United States), Cabot (Europe and United Kingdom, including debt servicing through Wescot) and LAAP (India subsidiary EARC and Mexico portfolios), which is not significant to results.
Q3 10-Q page:35 "Encore Capital Group, Inc. (“Encore”) has three business units: MCM"
Risk is concentrated in the United States; LAAP is too small to diversify.
Total debt purchasing revenue 525,457 (portfolio revenue 414,414 plus changes in recoveries 111,043), servicing revenue 17,474, other revenues 1,610, total 544,541 (US$ thousands).
Almost all revenue is debt purchasing revenue; about a fifth of Q3 revenue is forecast-driven changes in recoveries, which are non-cash and reversible.
United States 1,268,303, Europe 495,492, other geographies 5,007 of total 1,768,802 (US$ thousands).
The United States is the larger share of revenue and of purchasing; downside in the US collection environment is the main business risk.
Purchases depend on portfolio supply from issuers and mostly forward flow arrangements. Nine months 2026 purchases: MCM 998,024 and Cabot 198,287 (US$ thousands).
Supply is available now, but a decline in a major seller's volume would cut deployment; seller shares are not disclosed.
Management states supply is robust and pricing favorable.

Q3 10-Q page:36 "U.S. portfolio supply continues to be robust" and "pricing in the third quarter remained at favorable levels, although portfolio pricing was slightly higher compared to prior quarters"
Management characterisation, not adopted. Higher pricing lowers future returns on new vintages if collection assumptions do not rise.
Portfolio pricing competitive, which constrains European capital deployment.
Q3 10-Q page:37 "portfolio pricing remains competitive across our European footprint, constraining the amount of capital we elect to deploy in Europe"
Limits European growth; Europe contributes a smaller share of purchases.

Minimum aggregate purchase commitment under forward flow agreements of 684.5 US$m at 2026-09-30, with early termination or repricing rights; management expects actual purchases to be significantly greater.
Q3 10-Q page:30 "estimated minimum aggregate purchase price of $684.5 million"
Committed purchases are a cash call on liquidity, partly offset by contractual rights to reprice or terminate if quality deteriorates.
A significant percentage of purchases may be concentrated with a few large sellers; no seller share is stated.
10-K page:98 "may be concentrated with a few large sellers"
Missing datapoint: the share of purchases and collections by top sellers. It matters because loss of one seller would cut volume and pricing leverage. Not an adverse conclusion.
Call center and digital 1,089,064 and legal 621,023 for MCM; Cabot legal 177,338 and collection agencies 118,485 (US$ thousands).
Heavy reliance on litigation in the United States increases cost and conduct risk.
Largest operating costs are salaries (351,596) and cost of legal collections (286,220) for nine months 2026, with cost of legal collections up on increased US legal placements.
Q3 10-Q page:47 "Total cost of legal collections $ 286,220 $ 227,672 $ 58,548 25.7 %"
Cost of legal collections rises with the legal channel, so incremental collections carry rising court and fee costs.
Purchases of property and equipment 18,051 for nine months 2026; the main capital deployment is receivable portfolio purchases (1,187,072 net of put-backs).
Q3 release page:5 "Purchases of property and equipment (18,051) (19,338)"
Reinvestment need is dominated by portfolio purchases, which sit outside Adjusted EBITDA (see the financial base handoff).
No working capital metric is stated; operating liabilities and other assets moved by small amounts in the cash flow statement.
Q3 10-Q page:5 "Accounts payable, accrued liabilities and other liabilities 31,685 26,339"
Not disclosed as a measure; working capital is not a stated driver, so cash conversion depends on collections timing.

Collections above forecast and increases in expected future recoveries produce changes in recoveries revenue: 150,984 recoveries above forecast and 93,914 change in expected future recoveries for nine months 2026. Management concluded the over-performance did not represent a material shift in timing.
Q3 10-Q page:18 "Recoveries above forecast $ 51,827 $ 61,459 $ 150,984 $ 140,674" and "did not represent any material shift in timing of the collections"
Sustained over-performance has raised forecasts for recent vintages. If collections fall back, forecast cuts reduce revenue and Adjusted EBITDA while debt stays.
Collections in the United States have historically tended to be somewhat higher in the first three calendar quarters than in the fourth.
10-K page:12 "Collections in the United States have historically tended to be somewhat higher in the first three calendar quarters"
Q4 liquidity and cash interest timing should be read with this pattern.
Highly competitive; compete on price, ease of closing, funding and reputation; management believes compliance cost favors larger participants.
10-K page:13 "We believe this favors larger participants in this market"
Management belief; it supports scale as a credit factor but is not independently evidenced.
Management raised 2026 guidance: portfolio purchases 1.50 to 1.55 US$bn, collections 2.90 to 2.95 US$bn, EPS 15.50 to 16.00 US$.
Q3 release page:1 "we are raising our full-year 2026 guidance"
Forward-looking management claim; not evidence of outcome.

runs.text: Strengths. (1) Earnings momentum: last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 831,829 thousand and collections and portfolio balances grew [CP-1]; Documentary Fact. (2) Long-dated secured note stack with a lower coupon after the 2026 refinancings and no scheduled maturity before 2028 in the notes tables [CP-1] [CP-1A: Transaction summary]; Documentary Fact. (3) Demonstrated market access through repeated 2025 and 2026 issuance and a revolver maturing in 2029 [CP-1] [CP-1A: Timeline]; Documentary Fact, with the implication a reading of the record, so Analyst Interpretation. (4) Cash interest cover of 3.07x on a last twelve months basis [CP-1]; Documentary Fact. (5) Large US purchasing platform with a forward flow base that provides purchase visibility, with a minimum commitment of USD 684.5 million [CP-1A: Forward flow commitments]; Documentary Fact. Management's statements that competitive scale favors larger participants are carried as Management Language and not adopted [CP-1A: Competition].

Weaknesses. (1) Leverage remains high at 5.13x total debt to Adjusted EBITDA and 4.94x net [CP-1]; Documentary Fact. (2) Earnings quality: forecast-driven revenue inside Adjusted EBITDA and purchases outside it [CP-1] [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk]; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation. (3) Narrower revolver headroom of USD 510.2 million, a revolver that funds purchases, refinancing and repurchases, and a revolver ranking ahead of the notes on shared collateral enforcement [CP-1]; Documentary Fact, with the ranking a mechanic and not a recovery conclusion. (4) Legal-channel dependence and continuing regulatory exposure, including state Attorney General discussions [CP-1A: Legal and regulatory], [CP-1A: Collection channels, nine months 2026]; Documentary Fact. (5) Unmeasurable items: covenant headroom, seller concentration, large holders, target leverage and ratings [CP-0] [CP-1A: Concentration of sellers]; Insufficient Information, stated as gaps and not as adverse conclusions.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no sponsor transaction, merger, disposal or leveraged recapitalisation in the sources; the transaction record is financing activity only, and each item is completed unless stated. In the fourth quarter of 2025 the company issued 500.0 US$m of 6.625% Senior Secured Notes due April 2031 at an issue price of 100.000% and used a portion of proceeds to pay down revolver drawings (10-K page:69 "we issued $500.0 million 6.625% in senior secured notes that mature in 2031"); settled its 100.0 US$m 2025 convertible notes in cash for 106.2 US$m using revolver borrowings (10-K page:109 "In October 2025, the Company settled its $100.0 million 2025 Convertible Notes"); and repaid 100.0 EUR m of the 2028 Floating Rate Notes with revolver borrowings in November 2025 (10-K page:70). In 2026, on 2026-05-22 the company issued 750.0 US$m of 6.625% Senior Secured Notes due June 2032 at 100.000% and used proceeds to redeem in full the 500.0 US$m 9.250% notes due 2029, with a loss on extinguishment of 28.0 US$m including a 23.1 US$m make-whole premium (Q3 10-Q page:22 "Encore 2032 Notes"). On 2026-05-28 it issued 325.0 EUR m of floating rate notes due July 2033 at three-month EURIBOR plus 3.250% and, with revolver drawings, redeemed the 415.0 EUR m 2028 Floating Rate Notes, with a loss on extinguishment of 2.5 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:22). The nine month loss on extinguishment of 30,533 thousand is the sum of these two items and was booked in Q2 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:3). Management said the Q2 result absorbed 1.00 US$ per share of refinancing costs (Q2 release page:1 "includes $1.00 per share of refinancing costs"), which is management language. On 2026-07-22 the company called its 230.0 US$m 4.000% convertible notes due 2029 and on 2026-09-24 settled them in cash for 367.9 US$m funded by revolver borrowings, unwinding the capped call hedges for 31.8 US$m of proceeds; the 137.9 US$m excess over principal was charged to equity (Q3 10-Q page:24). On 2026-08-17 the U.S. Facility was extended from October 2028 to October 2029 and its margin reduced from 3.50% to 3.00% (Q3 10-Q page:25). In October 2026, after the balance sheet date and before the cutoff, new interest rate swaps with 150.0 US$m notional replaced swaps that matured on 2026-10-27 (Q3 10-Q page:14). The use of proceeds was refinancing in every case; the effect on liquidity and leverage is that debt rose over 2026 and revolver availability fell to 510.2 US$m at 2026-09-30 (financial base handoff). In the equity-side actions, the company repurchased 73.4 US$m of stock in the nine months to 2026-09-30 (Q3 10-Q page:58), expected to be funded from cash and revolver drawings. The company has not announced a pending transaction in the sources read, and the only acquisition-type event in the sources is the December 2024 step-up acquisition of EARC, with 11.3 US$m of goodwill recognised (10-K page:128).

fields.value: For ENCORE CAPITAL GROUP INC the filed statements support a clear financial base through Q3 2026, with the limits stated here. On the company's own Adjusted EBITDA, last twelve months leverage on gross debt fell from 5.96x at FY2025 to 5.13x at Q3 2026 and net leverage from 5.73x to 4.94x, because last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA grew from 676,958 to 831,829 (US$ thousands) while principal debt rose from 4,033,394 to 4,267,981. Cash interest cover on the same basis rose from 2.61x to 3.07x. Liquidity narrowed: the issuer-stated availability under the Global Senior Facility moved from 814.3 US$m at FY2025 to 510.2 US$m at Q3 2026 as the revolver funded the settlement of the 2029 convertible notes, and the other two debt facilities are fully drawn. The maturity profile is long: the notes tables show no instrument maturing before 2028, and the largest single maturity year is 2029 (the revolver and the U.S. Facility). The measure itself carries definition risk: roughly two fifths of nine month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA is revenue from changes in recoveries that the cash flow statement deducts as non-cash, and the large purchases of receivable portfolios needed to sustain collections sit in investing cash flow, outside both Adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow. Covenant headroom is not measurable because only limits and a compliance statement are printed. Overall this is a usable base for leverage, coverage and liquidity work, with Medium confidence on the headline ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For ENCORE CAPITAL GROUP INC the business is a consumer debt purchaser and collector that buys charged-off receivables at deep discounts, collects through call centers, digital channels and legal action, and recognises revenue from portfolio yield plus forecast-driven changes in recoveries. The United States business (MCM) is the dominant revenue and purchasing engine and Europe (Cabot, with the United Kingdom, France and Spain) is smaller and growing more slowly, with competitive pricing limiting European deployment. The company is a widely held listed company with no sponsor or controlling owner named in the sources, which removes sponsor extraction and sponsor support as drivers but leaves shareholder returns, funded in part from the revolver, as the capital allocation question. There is no live acquisition or sponsor transaction. The transaction record is a sequence of refinancings in 2025 and 2026 that extended the senior secured note maturities to 2031 to 2033 for the new issues, replaced a high coupon note, and, in the third quarter of 2026, retired the convertible notes in cash from revolver drawings; the effect on liquidity and leverage is in the financial base handoff. Credit-relevant business risks are forecast and pricing risk in a business where revenue recognition depends on collection forecasts, regulatory and litigation exposure that is continuing but not reserved, supply concentration among a few large sellers whose shares are not disclosed, and a heavy reliance on forward flow agreements that can be repriced or terminated. The view is Medium confidence because ownership, seller concentration and the executed financing terms are not in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no sponsor transaction, merger, disposal or leveraged recapitalisation in the sources; the transaction record is financing activity only, and each item is completed unless stated. In the fourth quarter of 2025 the company issued 500.0 US$m of 6.625% Senior Secured Notes due April 2031 at an issue price of 100.000% and used a portion of proceeds to pay down revolver drawings (10-K page:69 "we issued $500.0 million 6.625% in senior secured notes that mature in 2031"); settled its 100.0 US$m 2025 convertible notes in cash for 106.2 US$m using revolver borrowings (10-K page:109 "In October 2025, the Company settled its $100.0 million 2025 Convertible Notes"); and repaid 100.0 EUR m of the 2028 Floating Rate Notes with revolver borrowings in November 2025 (10-K page:70). In 2026, on 2026-05-22 the company issued 750.0 US$m of 6.625% Senior Secured Notes due June 2032 at 100.000% and used proceeds to redeem in full the 500.0 US$m 9.250% notes due 2029, with a loss on extinguishment of 28.0 US$m including a 23.1 US$m make-whole premium (Q3 10-Q page:22 "Encore 2032 Notes"). On 2026-05-28 it issued 325.0 EUR m of floating rate notes due July 2033 at three-month EURIBOR plus 3.250% and, with revolver drawings, redeemed the 415.0 EUR m 2028 Floating Rate Notes, with a loss on extinguishment of 2.5 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:22). The nine month loss on extinguishment of 30,533 thousand is the sum of these two items and was booked in Q2 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:3). Management said the Q2 result absorbed 1.00 US$ per share of refinancing costs (Q2 release page:1 "includes $1.00 per share of refinancing costs"), which is management language. On 2026-07-22 the company called its 230.0 US$m 4.000% convertible notes due 2029 and on 2026-09-24 settled them in cash for 367.9 US$m funded by revolver borrowings, unwinding the capped call hedges for 31.8 US$m of proceeds; the 137.9 US$m excess over principal was charged to equity (Q3 10-Q page:24). On 2026-08-17 the U.S. Facility was extended from October 2028 to October 2029 and its margin reduced from 3.50% to 3.00% (Q3 10-Q page:25). In October 2026, after the balance sheet date and before the cutoff, new interest rate swaps with 150.0 US$m notional replaced swaps that matured on 2026-10-27 (Q3 10-Q page:14). The use of proceeds was refinancing in every case; the effect on liquidity and leverage is that debt rose over 2026 and revolver availability fell to 510.2 US$m at 2026-09-30 (financial base handoff). In the equity-side actions, the company repurchased 73.4 US$m of stock in the nine months to 2026-09-30 (Q3 10-Q page:58), expected to be funded from cash and revolver drawings. The company has not announced a pending transaction in the sources read, and the only acquisition-type event in the sources is the December 2024 step-up acquisition of EARC, with 11.3 US$m of goodwill recognised (10-K page:128).

fields.value: Encore Capital Group's credit profile is improving but still highly levered: earnings and collections have grown faster than debt through 2026, yet the company remains a refinancing-dependent debt purchaser. The strongest support is last twelve months leverage of 5.13x total debt to Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026, down from 5.96x at FY2025, with cash interest cover of 3.07x, no scheduled maturity before 2028 in the notes tables and a long-dated senior secured note stack. The weakest point is earnings quality and liquidity: Adjusted EBITDA includes forecast-driven revenue, portfolio purchases sit outside it, and revolver availability fell to USD 510.2 million after the convertible notes were settled in cash. What decides the outcome is whether collections keep beating forecasts and whether the revolver is rebuilt rather than drawn further. [CP-1] [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Leverage fell on the company's own measure while debt rose. Evidence: total debt to Adjusted EBITDA moved from 5.96x at FY2025 to 5.13x at Q3 2026 on a last twelve months basis, with principal debt rising from USD 4,033,394 thousand to USD 4,267,981 thousand and last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA rising from USD 676,958 thousand to USD 831,829 thousand [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: the gain comes from earnings growth, not from debt reduction. Credit implication: leverage is falling because collections are strong; it would rise again if earnings fell, since debt is not being repaid. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Cash interest cover improved and is adequate on a last twelve months basis. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA over cash paid for interest was 3.07x at Q3 2026 against 2.61x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: cash interest is paid on semi-annual coupon dates, so single quarters mislead and the last twelve months basis is the right one. Credit implication: debt service is covered more than three times on the company measure, but the measure is before the portfolio purchases that sustain collections. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Revolver headroom narrowed after the convertible settlement. Evidence: issuer-stated availability under the Global Senior Facility moved from USD 814.3 million at FY2025 to USD 510.2 million at Q3 2026, the revolver draw rose from USD 691,648 thousand at Q2 2026 to USD 974,763 thousand at Q3 2026, and utilisation was 65.6% against 42.6% at FY2025; the other facilities are drawn to their commitments [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: purchases, refinancing and share repurchases are all funded from the revolver, and the loan to value covenant applies once utilisation exceeds 20%, so it is live. Credit implication: liquidity is thinner than a year ago and covenant headroom cannot be measured. Category: Documentary Fact; the covenant gap is Insufficient Information.

fields.value: 4. Adjusted EBITDA quality is the central definition risk. Evidence: nine month 2026 changes in recoveries of USD 244,898 thousand are 38.0% of nine month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 644,320 thousand, and are deducted as non-cash in operating cash flow of USD 159,630 thousand, while purchases of USD 1,187,072 thousand sit in investing cash flow [CP-1]; management concluded over-performance did not represent a material shift in timing, which is Management Language [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk]. Risk mechanic: revenue depends on forecast revisions that can reverse. Credit implication: headline leverage and cover overstate the cash left for debt service after reinvestment. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. The maturity profile is long but concentrated in 2029. Evidence: no instrument in the notes tables matures before 2028, USD 331.6 million of sterling notes matures in 2028, and USD 1424.8 million (the revolver and the U.S. facility) matures in 2029 [CP-1]; the 2026 refinancings replaced the 9.250% 2029 notes with 6.625% 2032 notes and extended the U.S. facility to October 2029 [CP-1A: Transaction summary]. Risk mechanic: the largest refinancing step is the secured bank-style funding that also supports daily purchasing. Credit implication: refinancing risk is back-ended but a single event, the 2029 renewal of both the revolver and the U.S. facility, matters. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Business risk centres on pricing, forecasts and the legal channel. Evidence: the business is dominated by debt purchasing revenue, United States purchasing is funded largely by forward flow agreements with a minimum commitment of USD 684.5 million, cost of legal collections rose 25.7% for nine months 2026 on higher US legal placements, and no material legal reserves are recorded [CP-1A: Revenue streams, Q3 2026], [CP-1A: Forward flow commitments], [CP-1A: Cost structure]. Risk mechanic: pricing and forecast errors flow into revenue; legal collections carry court cost and conduct risk. Credit implication: earnings are sensitive to collection performance and regulation, and seller concentration is Insufficient Information. Category: Documentary Fact; seller concentration is Insufficient Information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Governance gives creditors no sponsor support and no sponsor extraction. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder is named, there is no dividend history, share repurchases of USD 89.5 million in 2025 and USD 73.4 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 are expected to be funded partly from the revolver, and the refinancing record is repeated [CP-1A: Ownership and control], [CP-1A: Distributions]. Risk mechanic: shareholder returns compete with deleveraging for revolver capacity. Credit implication: capital allocation is a monitoring point; behaviour is Neutral or Mixed on documented actions only. Category: Documentary Fact for the actions, Analyst Interpretation for the behaviour label.

fields.value: Strengths. (1) Earnings momentum: last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 831,829 thousand and collections and portfolio balances grew [CP-1]; Documentary Fact. (2) Long-dated secured note stack with a lower coupon after the 2026 refinancings and no scheduled maturity before 2028 in the notes tables [CP-1] [CP-1A: Transaction summary]; Documentary Fact. (3) Demonstrated market access through repeated 2025 and 2026 issuance and a revolver maturing in 2029 [CP-1] [CP-1A: Timeline]; Documentary Fact, with the implication a reading of the record, so Analyst Interpretation. (4) Cash interest cover of 3.07x on a last twelve months basis [CP-1]; Documentary Fact. (5) Large US purchasing platform with a forward flow base that provides purchase visibility, with a minimum commitment of USD 684.5 million [CP-1A: Forward flow commitments]; Documentary Fact. Management's statements that competitive scale favors larger participants are carried as Management Language and not adopted [CP-1A: Competition].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. (1) Leverage remains high at 5.13x total debt to Adjusted EBITDA and 4.94x net [CP-1]; Documentary Fact. (2) Earnings quality: forecast-driven revenue inside Adjusted EBITDA and purchases outside it [CP-1] [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk]; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation. (3) Narrower revolver headroom of USD 510.2 million, a revolver that funds purchases, refinancing and repurchases, and a revolver ranking ahead of the notes on shared collateral enforcement [CP-1]; Documentary Fact, with the ranking a mechanic and not a recovery conclusion. (4) Legal-channel dependence and continuing regulatory exposure, including state Attorney General discussions [CP-1A: Legal and regulatory], [CP-1A: Collection channels, nine months 2026]; Documentary Fact. (5) Unmeasurable items: covenant headroom, seller concentration, large holders, target leverage and ratings [CP-0] [CP-1A: Concentration of sellers]; Insufficient Information, stated as gaps and not as adverse conclusions.
